assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, trapping neutral atoms at the magic wavelength so that Doppler and recoil shifts vanish while thousands of atoms are interrogated at once, opened fractional uncertainties near 1e-18. This is precision atomic physics of the kind I know well; it enables tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: The magic-wavelength lattice concept is clearly Katori's, and Ye's group drove the demonstration of record stability and accuracy and the connection to frequency combs. Two laureates is a natural configuration; Hall and Hansch were already honoured in 2005 for the comb, and Wineland's ion clocks in 2012, so credit separation is manageable. Others (e.g. Lemonde, Ludlow, Kimble) are not on the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Many independent laboratories (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE, NPL) now operate and compare lattice clocks at the 1e-18 level; the physics is stable and mature, and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: The prize may be viewed as an extension of earlier clock and frequency-comb prizes, which could reduce its perceived novelty.
Allocation relative to ion-clock and Sr/Yb contributions from other groups is a judgment call I cannot verify.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Tunable interactions through Feshbach resonances produced the BEC-BCS crossover and a strongly interacting, scale-invariant fermionic superfluid, with vortices, the universal equation of state and the unitary gas as a model of strongly correlated matter ranging from neutron stars to high-Tc systems. This is fundamental quantum many-body physics with a clean connection between experiment and theory.
assessment.attribution: Grimm (molecular BEC and crossover, collective modes, pairing gap), Salomon (collective oscillations, thermodynamics and the equation of state), and Zwierlein (vortices, superfluid transition, spin-imbalanced gases) were decisive, along with Jin and Ketterle whose roles are uncertain or not credited. John E. Thomas is excluded from my three, though his early unitary-gas work was important. With Jin deceased, the three-person split is delicate.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many groups over about two decades, with quantitative agreement with quantum Monte Carlo and theory; mature and stable.
uncertainties: Four credited people cannot all be honoured, and the omission of Thomas or any of the others will be contested.
Debt to the 2001 BEC prize and the late Deborah Jin's role complicate how to word the citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposals for quantum computing with trapped ions and, more broadly, for quantum simulation and quantum communication with atoms and photons laid the conceptual groundwork for a large part of modern AMO quantum technology. The ideas are original, clear and have been realised in the laboratory.
assessment.attribution: The partnership of Cirac and Zoller is long-standing and the credit between them is clean, with only two names to consider. Experimental demonstration is largely by others (Wineland, Blatt, Monroe), so a prize for the theory has to be framed as a proposal prize.
assessment.maturity: Realised repeatedly in ion, atom and photonic platforms; the field has matured greatly but the theory-only recognition question remains open given that Wineland was honoured in 2012.
uncertainties: Overlap with the separate trapped-ion and optical-lattice simulation candidates makes the proper framing uncertain.
Whether the committee wishes to honour theory-only proposals ahead of the experiments is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at magic twist angles in bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulator and superconducting states opened a genuinely new, tunable platform for strongly correlated physics. The result was unexpected in the way I value, and it has spawned moire physics in many materials.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 continuum-model prediction of the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity. That is a clean theory-plus-experiment split, though Cory Dean's group and others also contributed to the field around this time.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups worldwide within a few years, but the nature of the superconductivity and correlated states is still being debated. I would regard recognition as slightly early, though the central discovery is solid.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity is unresolved, so the interpretation is not yet stable.
Treatment of other experimental groups (e.g. Dean, Young, Efetov) and of others working on moire flat bands is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The geometric phase and the Aharonov-Bohm and Aharonov-Anandan phases are deep and unexpected insights into quantum mechanics, showing that quantum states carry memory of the path taken in parameter space. The concept now underpins molecular physics, optics, Berry curvature and topological band theory.
assessment.attribution: Berry's 1984 adiabatic phase is the decisive step, extended by Aharonov and Anandan to non-adiabatic cases, with Aharonov-Bohm separately foundational. Simon, Wilczek, Zee and Pancharatnam and Longuet-Higgins also bear on priority, and the Aharonov-Bohm part involves Bohm, now deceased, and Ehrenberg and Siday.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed experimentally in many systems (molecules, optics, NMR, solids) and conceptually mature for four decades; recognition is overdue rather than premature, with age a practical consideration.
uncertainties: Credit questions around Pancharatnam, Longuet-Higgins, Simon and Aharonov-Bohm precursors are historically subtle.
As a concept rather than one decisive experiment, it is harder to cast as a single discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator introduced a new classification of band insulators with protected edge and surface states. The prediction by Kane and Mele and the discovery in HgTe wells by Molenkamp's group are the kind of fundamental, unexpected insight into matter I appreciate. I defer to condensed matter colleagues on the finer points.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the Z2 and quantum spin Hall predictions; Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposed HgTe and Molenkamp's group observed it. Bernevig, Zhang (deceased), Hasan and others are not on this list, so the supplied credit is a plausible but incomplete picture.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by independent laboratories with ARPES and transport; well established and mature, with clear timing.
uncertainties: Competing credit for three-dimensional topological insulators (Fu, Kane, Mele, Moore, Balents, Hasan) is not captured by this list.
Overlap with the other topological candidates complicates configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics created strong light-matter coupling on a chip, the basis for dispersive readout and for superconducting-qubit processors. It is clear and elegant: an artificial atom coupled to a single microwave photon in a resonator, which echoes the cavity QED I know from atomic physics.
assessment.attribution: Blais proposed the architecture with Schoelkopf and Girvin, and Wallraff demonstrated strong coupling in 2004. Girvin is not credited here, and the prize configuration would depend on how contributions are apportioned.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced and now industrially central; however, the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits is recent and might make another circuit prize premature.
uncertainties: Proximity to the 2025 prize and the status of Girvin and of the transmon inventors (Koch, Schreier and others) make attribution unsettled.
The balance between fundamental discovery and technology is hard to judge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Programmable arrays of single Rydberg atoms in optical tweezers allow strongly interacting many-body quantum simulation and gate operations, with observed quantum phases and quantum-scar dynamics. These bring AMO physics into the many-body regime and are impressive, though I do not yet regard them as a completed discovery.
assessment.attribution: Browaeys (and Lahaye) and Lukin's group demonstrated the arrays and Rydberg blockade quantum simulation, and Saffman contributed the gate proposals along with Jaksch and Zoller, who are not credited here. Allocation is therefore uncertain.
assessment.maturity: The platform is still developing rapidly; confirmation across several groups is strong, but long-term stability of the main results is unknown, so recognition would be premature compared with older candidates.
uncertainties: Parts of the claim, especially error-corrected computation, remain under development.
Credit relative to Jaksch, Zoller and Bernien/Endres/Greiner and others is uncertain.
